small_guidance:
- Increase BLOCK_P to cover all pooled positions (PD*PH*PW = 7*31*31 = 6727, but per-(n,oc) you can use BLOCK_P=256 or 512 with proper masking) and raise num_warps to 8 since the inner sum is wide; also try num_stages=3.
- Avoid the atomic_add across OC by launching grid=(N,) and looping oc inside the kernel, accumulating bias contribution into a scalar register and writing once — eliminates 16-way contention on out[n].
- Hoist weight loads: pre-load the full (IC*KD*KH*KW = 216) weight vector for the current oc into registers once per program (outside the BLOCK_P loop), instead of reloading inside the 8×IC×KD×KH×KW nested loop.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as im2col-style GEMM: for each (n, oc) the conv produces OD*OH*OW = 14*62*62 outputs; fuse conv+div+maxpool by having one program compute a tile of pooled positions, gathering the 2×2×2 conv outputs directly. Treat K = IC*KD*KH*KW = 216 as the GEMM-K dim and reduce with tl.dot over BLOCK_K=32 tiles using a [BLOCK_P, BLOCK_K] x [BLOCK_K, 1] matmul (or pack OC into BLOCK_N to amortize input loads across all 16 output channels in one program).
- Better: one program per (n, pooled-tile), loop over all OC inside the kernel so the input window (shared across OC) is loaded once and reused for all 16 output channels; accumulate the per-pooled-position max, then do the global-avg + bias + sum-over-oc reduction in registers and write a single scalar per n.
- Use channels-last-ish layout for x (N, D, H, W, IC) so the IC reduction is the contiguous axis, enabling vectorized 8-wide loads (IC=8 fits one float8 vector) and letting tl.dot consume IC as the inner GEMM-K stride.
